AFDLWX

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Baltimore MD/Washington DC
1012 AM EDT Sun Oct 4 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
The main shield of rainfall looks to be staying south of the
I-95 metros. However, areas of drizzle will continue to be an
issue for much of the region, with widespread low stratus in
place.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
- 1) A frontal system nearby will maintain rain chances today
  with below average temperatures.

- 2) Frost and freezing temperatures are possible to the west of
  the Blue Ridge early next week.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1...A frontal system nearby will maintain rain
chances today with below average temperatures.

A frontal boundary remains stalled across the coastal Carolinas
back down across the southern U.S. Despite the local area being
in a stable post-frontal air mass, the atmosphere remains rather
moist per the 12Z IAD sounding (~1.25 inch precipitable water
value). This sounding showed much of the moisture in the surface
to 700-mb layer, with immense mid-level dry air above. In the 
net, this is supporting a thick area of low stratus across the 
entire region. This is being accompanied by patchy areas of 
drizzle, although some more concentrated shower activity has 
developed near I-64. Expect this to track northeastward in time 
which would move this activity into southern Maryland within the
next couple hours. Some additional precipitation may develop 
further to the north as well.

A persistent northeast wind should keep temperatures on the 
cool side widespread today into tonight. Highs will be mainly in
the 60s. Any rain chances should come to an end around this 
evening. Overnight conditions should be similar to last night 
with lows again in the 50s.

As a deep upper trough tracks across far eastern Canada, a more
potent cold front sweeps through the northeastern U.S. on
Monday. This will favor increasing sunshine, but also a large
uptick in northwesterly winds. Afternoon gusts up to 20 to 25
mph are possible, but with highs returning to the upper 60s to
mid 70s (upper 50s to 60s in the mountains).


KEY MESSAGE 2...Frost and freezing temperatures are possible to
the west of the Blue Ridge early next week.

A strong area of high pressure will build over the area next 
week, leading to an extended period of dry conditions. As a cooler 
airmass works in and high pressure builds overhead, frost and 
freezing temperatures may be possible to the west of the Blue Ridge 
both Monday night and Tuesday night. We'll start to see slightly 
warmer air build in from the south and west later in the week. High 
temperatures at lower elevations are forecast to be in the 60s 
(upper 50s/low 60s mountains) on Tuesday, upper 60s to low 70s on 
Wednesday (60s mountains), and mid 70s (mid-upper 60s mountains) on 
Wednesday and Thursday. Low temperatures will gradually moderate 
from the 30s/40s early in the week, to the upper 40s/low 50s later 
in the week.

&&

.AVIATION /13Z SUNDAY THROUGH THURSDAY/...
Lower ceilings and visibility through mid-morning as drizzle,
patchy fog, and pockets of light rain encompass much of the
eastern two-thirds of the region. MVFR to IFR conditions would
be the flavor.

Rain likely continues through the first half of today before a 
drying trend before dark. Low ceilings likely persist into
tonight given persistent northeasterly flow. However, VFR 
conditions return for Monday behind a strong cold front. Gusts 
up to 20 to 25 knots are possible during the afternoon hours.

VFR conditions are expected on both Tuesday and Wednesday. 
Winds are forecast to be out of the north on Tuesday, and then 
south on Wednesday.

&&

.MARINE...
Gusts up to around 10 to 15 knots are expected across the
Chesapeake Bay this morning before diminishing a bit later in
the day. Prevailing winds will mainly be out of the north to
northeasterly direction given the CAD wedge in place. The true 
ramp up in wind fields comes for the second half of Monday 
behind a cold front. Small Craft Advisories will likely be 
needed midday Monday through the night.

Sub-SCA level northerly winds are expected on Tuesday. Wind shift 
to out of the south on Wednesday, and are expected to remain sub-SCA 
in nature.

&&

.TIDES/COASTAL FLOODING...
Tidal anomalies have risen quite a bit over the last 6 to 12
hours with current values around 1 to 1.25 feet. This is
bringing some of the more sensitive locations into Action stage.
The forecast ahead shows anomalies remaining elevated through
early portions of the week. However, do expect some drop off
with the shift to northwesterly winds behind Monday's cold
frontal passage.

&&

.LWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
DC...None.
MD...None.
VA...None.
WV...None.
MARINE...None.

&&

$$

MARINE...BRO/KLW/KJP
